---
title: "Codebook & Methodology"
---

This page summarizes the full CONDLA codebook (`CONDLA_indices_codebook_v1.pdf`, downloadable from [Downloads & Replication](descargas.qmd)). It covers 28 Conditional Cash Transfer programs in 16 Latin American countries, 336 program-country-year observations between 1997 and 2026.

## The concept of conditionality, in three levels

Following Goertz's (2006) framework for concept structure in the social sciences, CONDLA treats welfare conditionality as a three-level concept:

- **Primary level**: the concept itself, *welfare conditionality*.
- **Secondary level**: three attributes — **behavioral requirements**, **monitoring**, and **sanctions** — individually necessary and, jointly, sufficient. Because they are assumed to interact (a high value on one does not compensate for the absence of another), they are aggregated with a **geometric mean**.
- **Tertiary level**: the concrete indicators for CCTs — education, health (by age group), workshops and labor on the behavioral side; monitoring frequency, binding agreements and evidence of compliance on the monitoring side; sanction severity for non-compliance with each behavioral condition on the sanctions side.

## The 36 coded variables, by dimension

| Dimension | Sub-dimension | Coded variables |
|---|---|---|
| Behavioral conditions | Education | `edu_mat_asis_res_cond` |
| | Health (by age group) | `salud_carn_vac_cond`, `salud_cont2_cond`, `salud_cont25_cond`, `salud_cont618_cond`, `salud_cont_adult_cond`, `salud_cont_pre_nat_cond` |
| | Labor and workshops | `lab_req_cond`, `lab_tall_cond` |
| | Level of detail | `otros_det_exp_cond` |
| Sanctions | Education (first/second non-compliance, most severe) | `edu_1er_inc_sanc`, `edu_2do_inc_sanc`, `edu_mas_severa_sanc` |
| | Health, by age group (same pattern ×5 groups) | `salud_{2,25,618,adult,pre_nat}_{1er_inc,2do_inc,mas_severa}_sanc` |
| | Other behaviors | `otras_cond_{1er_inc,2do_inc,mas_severa}_sanc` |
| | Level of detail | `edu_det_exp_sanc`, `otros_det_exp_sanc` |
| Monitoring | Frequency and detail | `frec_cont_mon`, `det_exp_mon` |
| Target population | Age groups covered | `grupos_po` (constructed, not directly coded) |

## How the indices are built

**Behavioral conditions.** Each sub-dimension is rescaled to 0-7 and combined with fixed weights (education and health together account for 91% of the weight, as the core components of CCTs):

$$
\text{behaviour} = 0.455 \cdot \text{cond\_edu} + 0.455 \cdot \text{cond\_health} + 0.045 \cdot \text{cond\_workshops} + 0.045 \cdot \text{cond\_labour}
$$

$$
\text{behaviour\_ind} = \text{behaviour} / 7
$$

**Monitoring.** Based solely on monitoring frequency, rescaled to 0-7:

$$
\text{monitoring\_ind} = \text{freq} / 7
$$

**Sanctions.** For each sanctionable domain (education, health, other), the severity of the first non-compliance, the second, and the most severe sanction are averaged, and the three domains are then averaged:

$$
\text{sanctions\_ind} = \frac{\text{sanc\_edu} + \text{sanc\_health} + \text{sanc\_otros}}{3}
$$

**Overall index.** The three dimension indices are combined with a geometric mean:

$$
\text{stringency} = (\text{behaviour\_ind} \times \text{monitoring\_ind} \times \text{sanctions\_ind})^{1/3}
$$

**Specification of the rules.** Independently of how strict the rules are, a second set of variables measures how explicitly they are specified (0 = vague, 1 = explicit), averaged into `av_specification`.

## Observations without a stringency index (14 of 336)

Because of how the index is built (a geometric mean of three components, each sensitive to missing information), 14 of the 336 observations do not have a computable `stringency` value: 10 from Bolivia's Bono Juancito Pinto (2006-2015, monitoring frequency not coded), 3 from Costa Rica's Superémonos (2000-2002, education sanctions not coded), and 1 from Panama's Red de Oportunidades (2006). These rows are **not imputed**: they remain missing, both in the downloadable dataset and in the charts under [Explore the Data](explorar.qmd), so as not to assign a stringency level that the available information does not allow us to establish.
